source_title: 'No standing to lecture India': New Delhi hits out at Pakistan over minority rights at UN - The Times of India
source_excerpt: NEW DELHI: India slammed Pakistan at the United Nations, questioning Islamabad's record on religious freedom and the protection of minorities while pointing out its failure to safeguard vulnerable communities at home despite criticising New Delhi.Speaking during an interactive dialogue with the UN Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Religion or Belief on funeral rights in exceptional circumstances on Thursday, India's first secretary to the UN, Bhavika Mangalanandan, said, "In Pakistan, the number of minorities is shrinking, and their rights are regularly abused. A state that cannot ensure the safety of its own minorities has no standing to lecture India."She also said human suffering should not be used to serve political interests and called for a more impartial approach to reporting violations of religious freedom.The remarks come against the backdrop of concerns over alleged forced conversions, abductions and marriages involving minority girls in Pakistan, particularly in Sindh.Separately, experts cited by the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights warned that coercion and weak legal safeguards were enabling forced conversions through marriage, particularly among Hindu and Christian communities.The experts emphasised that conversion must be voluntary and that child marriage undermines consent under international
